page.running_head: Lib. III. Justinus Thrax & Tiberius II.

main_text.head: CAPUT XIV. DE JUSTINO THRACE ET TIBERIO II.
main_text.p: Iustinianum JUSTINUS Curopalates, seu praefectus praetorio, cuius ex fororis proprio filius erat, item conjux Sophia Theodorae Augustae nepos erat, exceptis Residuo gentibus quae in Persidem pertinebant, ... In prima, quae ab initio usque Cariensis ... extendit, Justinus ... Gentium ... populo ... in Rempublicam reduxit, eidemque donativum more ... Tiberium ... Eorum verius, legatis, ne Avares hostes ... reciperet, petentibus, ... Avarum ... pactum a Justiniano tributum exegerunt ... Lasas a Justiniano adversus ... conjugia leges abso-lvit, et ... matrimonia ... ex conjugium ... volui. Armenios & Iberos, a Persis ... ... ... in fidem receperat ... Romanis accelatum, quod tetrio ... Domino ... foret, exauctoravit. Infidi ... Justinum cognatum, supremum militiae Magistrum, fulpectum interfecit, et ... atque Aetherium & Addaeum Senatores adjecit. Bulgaros Thracium ... ... Tiberium trans Istorum removit. In Africa cum Mauris, & in Asia cum Persis, invitate prius in societatem Aethiopum Rege Areta, bella gessit.

page.notes: Much of the text is damaged, faded and overprinted by show-through; many words are illegible and have been left as best read, with uncertain readings not marked individually. The marginal notes on the right are small, faint and mostly illegible (references such as "Cariensis", "Justin. Lib. 4.", "cap. 3."); they are not reliably readable. The left-margin marks are too faint to read. The scan is badly degraded, so this transcription is approximate.
